# StreamDek Mobile — 18 August 2026

## Fixed

**Peer-to-peer sources start again**
The peer-to-peer engine was registered under a name it no longer had, so it never started and
every source that needed it reported that the local server had not come online. The engine now
starts as soon as a source asks for it.

**Premium services respond to their own controls**
Switching a service off, reordering it, or disconnecting it could do nothing at all — silently,
with the switch flicking back and no explanation — whenever the account was signed out or the
session had expired. Those changes now apply to the keys held on the device, and say so. Failures
are reported per service rather than swallowed, and a change refused because the service was never
saved to the account uploads the device's key and tries once more.

**The premium services page stops flickering**
Every switch reloaded the whole page, which disabled the controls mid-tap and let two quick
changes come back in the wrong order. The page now keeps what it already shows.

**Services no longer switch themselves back on**
Turning on "Save keys to your StreamDek account" uploads the keys this device holds, and that
upload was re-enabling every service that had been switched off. Each key now carries its own
state and position. *Requires the matching backend release.*

**Continue Watching poster cards line up**
A card whose title fitted on one line was shorter than its neighbours, leaving the row with a
ragged edge. Every card now takes the height of the tallest.

**Title pages in the Centered style fade into the page**
With a background colour taken from the artwork, the Centered hero still faded into black, which
left a dark band across the join. It now fades into the page colour, as the Classic style does.

**Room on a tablet**
The language picker and the settings sheets stretched the full width of a tablet, which left a
language's code stranded far from its name. Both are now bounded, as is the text on the
peer-to-peer loading screen.

## New

**Source badges name the service and say what will happen**
A source that a premium service already holds now reads "Ready · Premiumize" rather than
"Cached". Real-Debrid switched off the endpoint that answers this question, so its sources carry
no badge — which now means "nobody could be asked", not "this will not play". They play exactly
as before.

**Fewer wasted requests before playback**
A service that cannot be asked what it holds is no longer asked. Real-Debrid was being walked
through its library on every stream list, and again before every playback, to produce an answer it
cannot give.

**Sources reach more networks**
Four tracker addresses that work over ordinary web traffic have been added to the ones tried for
every source, so a network that only carries web traffic still has a way to find peers.

**Clearer wording when a source cannot be found**
The peer-to-peer engine now says whether it found nobody sharing a source or could not reach the
peer-to-peer network at all, instead of asking for another source in both cases.
